mechanism: Bisacodyl-induced electrolyte loss (potassium and magnesium) may be compounded by eplerenone's potassium-sparing effects, creating risk of hypokalemia or hyperkalemia depending on baseline renal function and electrolyte status.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes (potassium, magnesium) and renal function regularly; consider alternative laxatives (polyethylene glycol) if chronic bisacodyl use is needed; educate patient on signs of electrolyte imbalance.
